heroHeadline: FOMC April Minutes: Officials Explicitly Discussed Rate Hikes; Single-Family Housing Starts Plunge -9%; Oil Back to ~$107 as Iran Ceasefire Reports Fail to Hold; Warsh Day 7
heroSubtitle: On Thursday May 21, 2026 — Kevin Warsh's seventh day as Federal Reserve Chair — US housing data confirmed that record-high mortgage rates are materially suppressing home construction: April 2026 single-family housing starts plunged -9% to 930,000 (SAAR), the weakest print since mid-2025, even as the total starts figure of 1.465 million beat the 1.410 million consensus estimate on multi-family strength. The data point lands against the backdrop of the prior session's most significant macro development: the release of the Federal Reserve's April 28–29 FOMC meeting minutes on May 20, which revealed that a majority of officials warned the Fed may need to consider raising interest rates if inflation remains persistently above the 2% target. Governors Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan all opposed retaining any easing bias in the April statement — the most hawkish internal stance since the tightening cycle peak. Only Stephen Miran dissented in favor of a cut. The FOMC minutes represent a fundamental shift in the policy risk distribution: markets must now price not just a prolonged hold at 3.50–3.75%, but a genuine probability of rate hikes on top of the 30-year Treasury already at 5.18–5.20% (an 18-year high). Fed Governor Michael Barr publicly opposed Warsh's planned $6.7 trillion balance sheet reduction on May 20 (Axios), marking the first intra-Fed institutional conflict of the Warsh era. Meanwhile, the Iran ceasefire reports that briefly pushed Brent crude below $100/bbl on May 20 — sparking a +1.08% S&P 500 rally to 7,432.97 — proved unconfirmed on May 21: Brent surged back to approximately $107/bbl, and markets reversed with the S&P 500 down -0.41% and the Nasdaq -0.72%. Nvidia's record Q1 FY2027 earnings ($81.6 billion revenue, +85% year-over-year; Data Center +92%) released after May 20's close sent the stock -0.5% in after-hours despite the beat. The combined picture for recession risk: single-family housing sector contracting, FOMC rate hike discussion explicit, oil back at $107 on unresolved Iran conflict, 30-year Treasury sustained at 18-year highs, and Goldman (30%), JPMorgan (35%), Moody's Analytics (49%) recession probabilities compiled before the hawkish FOMC minutes signal — all pointing to a worsening stagflation trap ahead of the June 16–17 FOMC and July 23 Section 122 tariff cliff.
footerNote: Data sourced from US Census Bureau (April 2026 housing starts, released May 21, 2026), Federal Reserve FOMC April 28-29 minutes (released May 20, 2026), Bloomberg (FOMC minutes hawkish signal), Axios (Fed Governor Barr opposes Warsh QT, May 20), 247 Wall St. (market performance May 20-21), CNBC (Nvidia Q1 FY2027 earnings, Brent oil, May 21), Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED DGS30 (30Y Treasury 5.18-5.20%), Goldman Sachs / JPMorgan / Moody's Analytics (recession probabilities 30%, 35%, 49%).
